title: Genius Makers
subtitle: The Mavericks Who Brought AI to Google, Facebook, and the World
pitch: A New York Times reporter tells the story of deep learning's rise: the outsiders, the bidding wars, and the safety fears that came with success.

chapters.g: A dramatic opening scene from the race to hire the first deep learning researchers.
The early dream of neural networks and the first machines that could learn.
Early researchers, including Geoffrey Hinton, keep faith in neural networks.
Neural networks fall out of favour and the believers work on the margins.
Deep learning finally starts to work, in speech and image recognition.
The results that convinced the industry deep learning was real.
Big tech companies start chasing the researchers.
Google, Facebook, Microsoft and others compete for talent and breakthroughs.
Excitement and big promises around AI grow fast.
The skeptics push back on the hype.
AI spreads across products and research fields.
The labs grow and the stakes rise, including the founding of new labs focused on AGI.
Big visions of AGI and what it would bring.
Deepfakes and AI generated deception become real problems.
Overconfidence in what AI could do, and its failures.
Bias in AI systems and the researchers who exposed it.
Military uses of AI and the protests inside tech companies.
The limits of what companies and governments could control.
The argument over whether AI is an existential risk.
Robots, jobs and what machines still cannot do.
For some, AGI becomes almost a belief system.

ideas: Deep learning won after decades on the margins.
A handful of people and companies shaped modern AI.
Safety, bias and military use became fights inside the industry.

args.a: The story of AI is a story of people and incentives.
args.c: Readers looking for technical depth or a risk analysis will find this mostly a narrative history.

questions: What does the history of neural networks teach about ideas that seem dead?
How did competition between companies shape safety choices?

quiz.q: What kind of book is Genius Makers?
o: A narrative history of deep learning
quiz.w: It follows the people who built modern AI.

quiz.q: Which chapter covers the argument over existential risk?
quiz.w: Debate looks at whether AI is an existential risk.
